key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling passivant chemistry and surface stoichiometry offers a route to higher-efficiency methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Evaluate surface reconstruction, electron extraction into C60, and solar-cell performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term stability or manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
